title: Water security planning and energy costs for desalination
asked: Ms He Ting Ru asked for the latest assessment of Singapore's water insecurity risks, especially before the 2061 Johor Water Agreement expires, and what accelerated measures are planned so the Four National Taps meet future needs without hurting food production or household supply.
response: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien said PUB continues to plan ahead and invest in water infrastructure to meet future demand, taking into account economic and population growth and climate change, and that supply is diversified through the Four National Taps, including desalinated water and NEWater as weather-resilient sources. On energy, she said cost is a driver PUB has always paid attention to, that it has looked at ways to reduce energy use in water treatment, and that it set a goal for PUB to keep searching for new technology to bring down the overall cost of producing water, including energy.

key_points.point: PUB plans and invests ahead for future water demand, factoring in economic and population growth and climate change
key_points.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
key_points.quote: PUB continues to plan ahead and invest in water infrastructure to meet future demand, taking into account economic and population growth as well as the impact of climate change.

key_points.point: Water supply is diversified through the Four National Taps, with desalinated water and NEWater described as weather-resilient
key_points.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
key_points.quote: These include desalinated water and NEWater, which are weather-resilient sources that strengthen our water security amid the effects of climate change.

key_points.point: Energy cost is a factor PUB has consistently tracked
key_points.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
key_points.quote: With regard to cost of energy, it is definitely a driver that we have always paid attention to.

key_points.point: PUB has looked at reducing energy use in water treatment
key_points.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
key_points.quote: We have looked at ways to reduce our energy efficiency for water treatment.

key_points.point: Reducing the overall cost of producing water, including energy, was set as a goal for PUB to pursue through new technology
key_points.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
key_points.quote: we set that as our goal so that our PUB colleagues will focus their attention on always searching for new technology that will reduce the overall costs of producing water, including energy
